root_idea.summary: The root expresses two principal orientations: fullness or completion, and hastening toward or ahead of something.
root_idea.development: The fullness branch appears in the full moon, completed quantities, bodily fullness, and things reaching an early or foremost state. The haste branch develops into striving to precede, acting before a due point, and words, actions, tears, or events issuing suddenly.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic verbal-noun citation form بِدَارٌ.

senses.definition: Hastening to consume or spend something before a due point; in the Quranic construction, hastily using the property of wards before they reach maturity.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in بِدَارًا أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا, describing premature expenditure of orphan property by a guardian. The sense emphasizes acting ahead of the wards’ attaining maturity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full, as the moon; also to rise like the full moon. Of a boy, to become full-grown and rounded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical verb; the boy comparison is figurative, based on the fullness and roundness of the full moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of fruit, to attain maturity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or figurative extension recorded for fruit reaching its mature state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to give birth earlier in the year than other camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral usage concerning an unusually early birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go out to urinate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or euphemistic usage in the first-person expression خَرَجْتُ أَبْدُرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten to do, attain, or obtain something; to strive to be first or beforehand, including vying with another in hastening toward it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Immediate transitivity may express hastening toward the object; constructions with إِلَى or بِ need not by themselves imply mutual rivalry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an affair or event, to come upon someone quickly, suddenly, or before expected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which the event is the subject and its occurrence is characterized by speed or unexpected precedence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a saying or action, to proceed suddenly and hastily from someone without premeditation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially associated with an utterance or action issuing under sudden impulse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the full moon rise to or upon someone; by extension, to journey during a night of full moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The first use is a Form IV causative or inchoative expression associated with moonrise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an unripe date, to become red.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage for the color change of an unripe date.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten together; to vie with one another in haste or in being first.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction, often followed by a goal or the thing to be undertaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appear immediately or at first sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression هٰذَا مَا يَتَبَادَرُ مِنْهُ, referring to what is understood at the first impression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the eyes, to flow with tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily expression attested in the dual form اِبْتَدَرَتْ عَيْنَايَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heap up wheat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The full moon, especially the moon on its fourteenth night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun also denotes the full-moon night in لَيْلَةُ البَدْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lord, master, or chief of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation likening a prominent person to the full moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a boy, full of youthful vigor and flesh; full or plump, and in some usage precocious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a boy; it is distinct from the verbal use بَدَرَ ‘to become full-grown.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cover or a round dish or plate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on roundness and resemblance to the full moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Badr, a named place between Mecca and Medina, also described as a known water-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name, not the ordinary noun ‘full moon’; the name is explained as belonging to a man called Badr.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an eye, quick- or sharp-sighted, seeing before others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to an eye that perceives before the eyes of others, including a horse’s eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an eye, round, large, or full like the full moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative descriptive branch for the eye epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The skin of a weaned lamb or kid, used as a milk container.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term distinguishes the container from skins used before weaning or for clarified butter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large sum of money, especially ten thousand dirhams, or a purse containing a specified large number of dirhams or dinars.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usage varies among authorities as to the exact amount. In بَدْرَةٌ مُبَدَّرَةٌ, the second word reinforces the sense of an aggregated or completed sum.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vying with one another to outrun or outstrip each other in haste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression اِسْتَبَقْنَا البَدَرَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain that comes before, shortly before, or in the first part of winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A seasonal adjective describing early winter rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose mother gave birth earlier in the year than other camels, making her especially abundant and good in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral adjective derived from the notion of coming early.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fat young camel recently weaned from its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral noun or adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lamb born shortly before winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A seasonal pastoral term for an early-born lamb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where wheat or grain is trodden out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional agricultural term, especially associated with the dialect of Iraq.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wheat, straw, or reaped grain collected together at the threshing place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic extension from the place to the grain assembled there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place for drying dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A less common agricultural usage attributed to a lexical authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hastiness of temper; a sudden angry impulse, hasty utterance or action, slip, error, or sudden mischief issuing from anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural بَوَادِرُ is common for angry slips or rash words and actions; بَادِرَةُ الشَّرِّ denotes evil or harm that suddenly befalls someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intuitive knowledge, an immediate notion, or the faculty of judging or improvising rightly at the first occurrence of something unexpected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A positive intellectual sense, distinct from the angry impulse sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The point of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete sense of a projecting extremity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity of an arrow next to its head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for the part adjoining the arrowhead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The head or first emerging part of a plant, including the first part of the henna plant to appear as the earth opens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical sense referring to the earliest visible growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The leaves of the herb حُوَّاءَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The best and freshest growth of the plant وَرْس.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical usage for the most vigorous new growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fleshy portion between the shoulder joint and the neck; in the dual or plural, the corresponding fleshy portions or sides of an animal’s breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun with slightly different specifications for humans and camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foreparts or first portions of horses as they appear or suddenly come into view.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression referring to the foremost or initially visible parts of the horses.
